title: Execution Grant
description: The object an adapter presents to prove it may act (backlog E1-004, ADR-012). Signed over the ADR-011 canonical form of every field except the signature itself. It authorises one run against one pinned target: there is no session, no refresh and no renewal, so a grant that needs extending is a new decision rather than a longer one.

nonce.description: Single-use value the replay cache is keyed on. Hexadecimal and at least 128 bits, so it cannot be guessed and cannot be a counter.

key_id.description: Names the key that signed this grant, so rotation does not invalidate grants already in flight. A verifier holds an explicit set of trusted values and an unknown one is a refusal, never a fallback.

scope_hash.description: The immutable snapshot this grant authorises against. The scope is referenced, never restated, so a grant and the scope it claims cannot drift apart.

audience.description: The adapter identity permitted to present this grant. Presenting it as anyone else is a refusal.

run_id.description: The single run this grant belongs to, and the unit revocation acts on.

pinned_addresses.description: The exact addresses resolution authorised (E1-002). A connection to anything else is refused even while the grant is otherwise valid. Empty is not expressible: a grant that authorises no destination authorises nothing.

profile.description: There is no third value. Destructive tooling has no representation here, so it cannot be authorised by a grant however it is issued.

signature.description: Over the canonical bytes of every other field. Verified before the window and before revocation, so an unsigned document cannot probe which runs exist.

timestamp.description: UTC with a literal Z. An offset would let two grants describe the same instant differently and change the canonical bytes.

address.description: A resolved literal, never a name. A name here would have to be resolved again at connect time, which is the time-of-check to time-of-use gap E1-002 exists to close.
